CVE-2026-56392 is an integer overflow in unexpand buffer allocation that multiplies max_column_width by MB_LEN_MAX. That allocation path was introduced after coreutils 9.7 (multibyte expand/unexpand support; first present in 9.11). Debian trixie and this DHI package ship 9.7, which still allocates with ximalloc(max_column_width) and does not contain the vulnerable multiply.
The DHI coreutils package backports the upstream uniq -w multibyte find_field() fix from commit d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371.

Backported the upstream HTTP::Tiny 0.095 credentialed-redirect hardening (allow_credentialed_redirects / allow_downgrade defaults, plus protocol-relative Location handling) into the bundled HTTP::Tiny shipped by the DHI perl package. statements.action_statement: Use-after-free in xmlParseInternalSubset (DoS via crafted XML with improper entity resolution) affecting libxml2 2.9.11-2.11.0. The DHI package ships the Debian trixie 2.9.14 repack, which is in the affected range. Upstream fixed this only as a side effect of the entity-amplification rework in https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/463bbeeca1805b5c4828f50d0fefc4eebaf620df (v2.11.0): a large parser.c rewrite plus ABI-changing additions to the public entities.h and parser.h structures. There is no isolated upstream patch, and neither Debian nor Ubuntu ships a backport to their 2.9.x branches. The fix cannot be applied to the 2.9.14 source without breaking API/ABI version compatibility for consumers, so no patch is carried. Reference: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-6653

The patched HTTP::Tiny rejects CR, LF, and other control characters in the request method, Request-URI, the URL-derived Host header, and HTTP/1.1 control-field header values before they are written to the socket, so the header-injection / request-smuggling behavior is mitigated inline.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress IO::Uncompress::Unzip _dosToUnixTime hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched _dosToUnixTime short-circuits to 0 for a zero DOS datetime and wraps Time::Local::timelocal() in an eval guard so out-of-range month/day/hour values no longer raise an uncaught exception out of IO::Uncompress::Unzip->new($file), so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.

Backported the upstream IO::Compress zipdetails hardening into the DHI perl package. The patched zipdetails CLI calls the correctly spelled unpackValue_Q helper when decoding 8-byte UID/GID values from Info-ZIP Unix Extra Fields (closing the published undefined-subroutine crash), and decode_ux now validates the UID/GID Size byte through canDecodeLittleEndian and reports invalid or zero sizes as bad data instead of triggering internalFatal, so the vulnerable behavior is mitigated inline.

NULL dereference in dri2GetGlxDrawableFromXDrawableId() inside libGLX_mesa.so only triggers when an X11 server sends an unexpected DRI2_BufferSwapComplete event to a GLX client. NVD and Debian mark this disputed with no reproducible scenario; Debian security tracker lists no fixed version and urgency unimportant. Exploitation requires a malicious or buggy X display server, not input reachable by remote attackers against headless pkg-mesa consumers using GBM/EGL/Vulkan.

Buffer over-read in glXQueryServerString() is only reachable from a GLX client parsing replies from an X11 display server. The CVE is disputed because no common use case requires uninterrupted operation against an attacker-controlled server; Debian lists it unfixed with unimportant urgency. pkg-mesa ships headless GPU libraries for container/server workloads and does not expose a remotely controllable X server attack surface.

Segmentation fault in glx_pbuffer.c __glXGetDrawableAttribute() requires a GLX client to query drawable attributes from a malicious X11 server response. Debian and NVD mark the report disputed; no fixed upstream or Debian version exists. Triggering the fault requires control of the X display server, which is outside adversary control in typical pkg-mesa headless deployments.

NULL dereference in check_xshm() for the GLX XShm extension is only exercised when a GLX client negotiates shared-memory transport with an X11 server. NVD notes the CVE is disputed with no demonstrated scenario; Debian tracker marks it unfixed and unimportant. An adversary cannot drive this path without supplying a malicious X server, which pkg-mesa server/container consumers do not rely on.
